sources.title: Principles of Membrane Transport
sources.publisher: Garland Science, in Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th edition, via NCBI Bookshelf
sources.locator: Permeability statements for small nonpolar molecules, small uncharged polar molecules and ions; the figure that synthetic bilayers are 10^9 times more permeable to water than to sodium or potassium; the channel and carrier mechanisms and their rate difference; the statement that all channel proteins and many carrier proteins allow only downhill passive transport, called facilitated diffusion; and the combination of concentration and electrical gradients into an electrochemical gradient.

sources.title: Na+/K+-ATPase: More than an Electrogenic Pump
sources.locator: Statements that in each cycle every functional unit of the pump extrudes three sodium ions and imports two potassium ions using the chemical energy obtained from ATP hydrolysis, and that this process results in the removal of a net positive charge per cycle, contributing to the establishment of a negative membrane potential.
sources.license: CC BY, stated on the article page; facts-only use with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to establish the pump's three-for-two-per-ATP cycle independently of the textbook source, and to establish that the pump is electrogenic and contributes to a negative membrane potential, which is what connects the pump to the voltage term in the lesson's own calculation. agentAccess.notes: Retrieved through the PMC articles route recorded as allowed in site/agent/source-access-ledger.json on the evidence that robots carries Allow: /articles/. Licence wording and both quoted statements confirmed on the article page.

sources.title: A general method for determining secondary active transporter substrate stoichiometry
sources.locator: Introductory statements that coupling stoichiometry, the stoichiometric ratio of coupling ion to substrate molecules transported per transport cycle, dictates the extent to which a substrate can be moved against its concentration gradient, and that by coupling the transport of one substrate molecule to several ions a transporter can generate a large substrate gradient.
sources.license: CC0 1.0 public domain dedication, stated on the article page; facts-only use with no source expression reused

sources.title: Intestinal sugar transport
sources.locator: Introduction: the phenomenon was considered secondary active transport as ATP hydrolysis was indirectly coupled to glucose transport via the electrochemical gradient; and glucose transport was blocked by ouabain, which inhibits the basolateral sodium-potassium ATPase that maintains the enterocyte sodium gradient and drives brush-border transporters such as SGLT1. SGLT1 section: the 2:1 stoichiometry and brush-border location. GLUT2 section: facilitative diffusion across the basolateral membrane.
sources.license: Copyright 2006 Baishideng Publishing Group Co., Limited. All rights reserved. Facts-only use with no source expression reused.

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only for the description of the coupling to ATP hydrolysis as indirect, the ouabain observation, GLUT2's facilitative diffusion across the basolateral membrane, and corroboration of the SGLT1 stoichiometry and location. The article reserves all rights, so no wording, figure, table or dataset was copied or adapted and every sentence in the lesson is original expression.

agentAccess.notes: Retrieved through the PMC articles route recorded as allowed in site/agent/source-access-ledger.json. The article also states that oral rehydration rests on SGLT1 cotransporting water; the lesson does not use that statement, because the water-cotransport question is contested and is handled from sources dedicated to it.

sources.license: CC BY 4.0, stated on the article page; facts-only use with no source expression reused

sources.title: Oral Rehydration Therapy in the Second Decade of the Twenty-first Century
sources.locator: Statements that most critical to the development of oral rehydration solution was that cholera enterotoxin, that is cyclic AMP, did not inhibit glucose-stimulated sodium and thus fluid absorption; that glucose stimulates sodium absorption via a cyclic-AMP-independent transport process despite the stimulation of active chloride secretion by cyclic AMP; and that subsequent studies identified the intestinal glucose-sodium transporter as SGLT1.
sources.license: CC BY, stated on the article page as the Creative Commons Attribution License; facts-only use with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only for the central mechanism of the lesson's clinical scene: that raised cyclic AMP does not inhibit glucose-stimulated sodium and fluid absorption, that the glucose-coupled route is cyclic-AMP-independent while chloride secretion is cyclic-AMP-stimulated, and that the transporter concerned is SGLT1. No wording, figure, table or dataset was copied or adapted despite the licence permitting it with credit.

agentAccess.notes: Retrieved through the PMC articles route recorded as allowed in site/agent/source-access-ledger.json. sources.title: Water transport controversies - an overview

sources.title: Routes of Epithelial Water Flow: Aquaporins versus Cotransporters
